evidence: Making a Better World is by Don Parson, catalogued as Donald Craig Parson. Both the 1983 Headline-Happy Public Housing War article and the 2007 Decline of Public Housing article are also by Don Parson: 10/10 listed citation counts.

Unicamp identifies José Luís Sanfelice as the author of Movimento estudantil (1986). He also coedited Liberalismo e educação em debate and Capitalismo, trabalho e educação and wrote História das instituições escolares. Luiz/Luís is a spelling variation; the malformed container citations do not establish a second Sanfelice.

Armed Struggle and the Search for State is by Yezid Sayigh, who also coedited The Cold War and the Middle East and The Third World Beyond the Cold War. The listed Palestine and police-reform publications are his as well. Ṣāyigh, Yazīd is the transliterated authority heading for the same author.

História da polícia civil de São Paulo is by Hermes Vieira and Oswaldo Silva (5 counts). A foice e a cruz is by Osvaldo Heller da Silva (4); Guerra y trueque is by Osvaldo Silva Galdames (1). The LC author therefore accounts for exactly half, not a predominant share.

Honor/Honour (8 counts together) and Fundamentals of age-group systems (1) are by Frank Henderson Stewart: 9/10. A Half Century of Municipal Reform (1) is by Frank Mann Stewart. Romare Bearden (0) is the photographer Frank Stewart’s book.

Donas de bens e de gentes (2) and As redes sociais dos homens-bons (1) are Regina Mendes de Araújo’s; Geografia do Brasil (1) is by Magnoli and geographer Regina Araújo. Anais carries 5/9 counts but cannot be uniquely identified from this generic title. No Renata work is confirmed; the zero share is provisional pending identification of Anais.

Integralismo is by Rosa Maria Feiteiro Cavalari. Educação e Integralismo is her doctoral research, and the 1987 Unicamp dissertation fragment corresponds to her Os limites do movimento estudantil, 1964–1980. The education/integralism writings belong to this same scholar; Feitero omits an i.

Patrick Joseph Healy (coauthor of A Statement for Non-Exclusion)
evidence: The National Library of Ireland explicitly catalogues The Chronicle of Hugh of Flavigny under Patrick Edward Healy, 1955– (5 counts); the Lanfranc article is also his (1): about two thirds of 9. The 1932 Mysticism article is by Patrick Joseph Healy, the Parks interview by journalist Patrick Healy, and the 1905 Non-Exclusion book by another Patrick J. Healy with Ng Poon Chew.

Le monde hellénistique and L’économie royale des Lagides are Claire Préaux’s books. Her bibliography also includes Esquisse d’une histoire des révolutions égyptiennes sous les Lagides and Polybe et Ptolémée Philopator. Cl. abbreviates Claire; all 14 listed citation counts belong to her.

Orlando Furioso and its Harington translation are works of the poet Ariosto, 1474–1533. The Morgan catalogues the 1591 English Heroical Verse edition under Lodovico while recording Ludovico on its engraved portrait. These are variants of the same given name; Le opere minori is also his.
